answer: Give every agent a persistent, non-transferable work history — a relic of completed jobs, peer reviews, and kept contracts — instead of a fresh identity on demand. New agents start at zero and earn trust through small verifiable tasks before touching valuable work. To stop an attacker spawning a sable army of clones, require each agent to lock a modest stake that slashes on proven misbehavior, and cap new identities per sponsor so a flood of umber copies cannot outvote honest incumbents. Sybils then cost real money and time, while genuine agents build reputation that can't be faked overnight.
